source: US adults with carcinoid syndrome: the US neuroendocrine tumour stock times the share with the syndrome. (1) THE STOCK: 'The estimated 20-year limited-duration prevalence of NETs in the United States on January 1, 2014, was 171 321' (Dasari A, Shen C, Halperin D et al., 'Trends in the Incidence, Prevalence, and Survival Outcomes in Patients With Neuroendocrine Tumors in the United States', JAMA Oncol 2017;3(10):1335-1342, doi 10.1001/jamaoncol.2017.0589, PMID 28448665, PMC5824320, SEER). (2) THE SHARE: '9512 eligible patients were diagnosed with NETs, of whom 1786 (19%) had carcinoid syndrome' (Halperin DM, Shen C, Dasari A et al., 'Frequency of carcinoid syndrome at neuroendocrine tumour diagnosis: a population-based study', Lancet Oncol 2017;18(4):525-534, doi 10.1016/S1470-2045(17)30110-9, PMID 28238592, PMC6066284, SEER-Medicare), 1786 / 9512 = 0.18776. Both read 2026-11-16. (3) 171,321 x 0.18776 = 32,168
note: THE POOL IS CARCINOID SYNDROME, NOT CARCINOID TUMOUR. The book's indication name is the tumour; NCT07087054 (CAREFNDR) treats the syndrome, 'Documented carcinoid syndrome requiring medical therapy' with more than one flushing episode a day, so the pool is the syndrome. THREE WAYS IT IS OFF, TWO OF THEM UPWARD: the stock is 2014 and NET prevalence was rising (Dasari: incidence up 6.4-fold from 1973 to 2012); Halperin's share is at diagnosis, in patients 65 and over, excluding pancreatic NETs and small-cell and large-cell lung cancer, and the syndrome also appears later as tumours spread to the liver; the one downward is that the stock includes pancreatic NETs, which rarely cause the syndrome. CONTEXT, NOT USED: Crinetics estimated '28,000-51,000 adults diagnosed with NETs are undergoing medical management. Of these, it is estimated that approximately 18,000-34,000 are candidates for treatment with paltusotine' (FY2025 10-K 0001658247-26-000012), a company estimate and not epidemiology

source: the US neuroendocrine tumour incidence on the Census population, times the same carcinoid syndrome share. (1) 'The age-adjusted incidence rate increased 6.4-fold from 1973 (1.09 per 100 000) to 2012 (6.98 per 100 000)' (Dasari 2017, PMID 28448665, as above). (2) 340,110,988 US residents at 2024-07-01, US Census Bureau Vintage 2024 National Population Estimates (nc-est2024-agesex-res.csv, the denominator the book already holds). (3) 6.98e-5 x 340,110,988 = 23,740 new NETs a year, x 0.18776 (Halperin 2017, PMID 28238592, as above) = 4,457
note: an age-adjusted rate applied to the crude population, which leans low for an older country than the 2000 standard. Halperin's share is the share with the syndrome at diagnosis, which is what an incidence wants, so the share fits this row better than the prevalence row above

The current SPL, DailyMed setid 44068127-f5c0-7e8b-e063-6294a90aea87 version 4 published 2026-10-21, is the one the book's labels table holds, with its indications text empty; read 2026-11-16, no carcinoid indication appears in any Palsonify SPL. NCT07087054 requires 'locally advanced or metastatic histopathologically confirmed well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor(s)' with carcinoid syndrome (registry, checked 2026-11-16)
note: a patient with both acromegaly and carcinoid syndrome exists (an ectopic GHRH-secreting NET) but is a case report, not a share

note: THIS LAYER IS STILL SHORT FOUR KEYS AND NONE COULD BE SOURCED FREE. With these five rows indication_layer.build should ask for eligible_pct, penetration_peak_pct, discontinuation_pct and net_price_per_patient (the last two because Palsonify's base model seeds no price or stopping rate). PRICE: Crinetics 'sells PALSONIFY at Wholesale Acquisition Cost' but never prints it (FY2025 10-K 0001658247-26-000012; 10-Q to 2026-06-30 0001658247-26-000053), and reports enrollment forms (245 in Q2 2026) and prescribers (385) but no patients on drug, so revenue cannot be divided into a price; Medicaid State Drug Utilization Data suppresses every national Palsonify row it holds (NDCs 84015-0920-60 and 84015-0930-60, 2025 Q4 and 2026 Q1, data.medicaid.gov datasets 158a1baa and 2957a7f9, queried 2026-11-16); CMS Part B and Part D 2024 predate the September 2025 launch. ELIGIBLE: the trial's bar (active flushing more than once a day, no telotristat need, no prior somatostatin non-response) has no free US share; Halperin reports octreotide use only as an odds ratio (18.5), not a share. PENETRATION: the only oral somatostatin analogue analogue, Mycapssa, is not reported separately by any filer, and Palsonify's own acromegaly launch is three quarters old
